texts.section_4_4: The comparison also reflects differences in interface restrictions. Both static arrangements prohibit DN-to-TN active-power flow, whereas coordinated operation uses reverse flow in four representative interface-hours. When this restriction was removed from the static arrangements, TN dispatch runs could not accommodate the prescribed DN exchanges in one of twelve representative year--season blocks for passive operation and eight for price-taker operation (Section~S5 of the supplementary material). To separate the two effects, coordinated operation was re-evaluated with the same no-reverse-flow restriction imposed on the consensus exchange. The restriction raises the coordinated cost by 20.5~k\euro{}, a determinate increase at 1.62 times its threshold, which is 0.02\,\% of the 90.9~M\euro{} saving: the saving relative to the price-taker arrangement is 12.2\,\% with reverse flow enabled and 12.2\,\% with it prohibited. The coordination benefit reported here does not depend on the interface restriction; it applies to the specific benchmark arrangements defined in Section~\ref{sec:case_settings}.
texts.section_4_7: The sensitivity of the decisive comparisons to the coordination penalties was tested by re-evaluating the plan without storage and the reference unit, at the base and at twice the base flexibility price, with every initial penalty parameter halved and doubled. All eight re-evaluations certified. Across the three penalty settings, the operating-cost difference between the two plans varied by 1.6~k\euro{} at the base price and 1.5~k\euro{} at twice the base price, about 0.12 of its determinacy threshold in each case, and every sign and verdict was unchanged; seven of the eight re-evaluations fell inside the acceptance window of the corresponding frozen evaluation and the eighth lay 0.7~k\euro{} above it. The check covers the penalty schedule, not the start of the coordination: a different initialisation could in principle reach a different local solution, and the limitation below stands.
texts.appendix_B4: More generally, at every certified evaluation behind the tables of Section~\ref{sec:results}, every penalised slack in $Q$ (daily closure, network feasibility and the agent's net-power pair) sits at its zero bound to within the solver's bound relaxation, so no penalty is paid in $Q$; the relaxation itself leaves a common offset of $-13.0$~k\euro{} in $Q$ ($-2 \times 10^{-5}$ of $Q$), identical across evaluations to within 40~\euro{}, which cancels in every reported difference. The multi-scenario evaluation of the reference unit carries a positive flexibility-balance content of at most 2.2~\euro{}, and the superseded evaluation~16 a positive voltage-slack content of at most 171~\euro{}.
texts.letter_benchmark_bullet: \item The uncoordinated benchmark was redefined. The submitted comparison let distribution networks export into a transmission network that has no load of its own; the revised benchmark gives the uncoordinated arrangements a no-reverse-flow interface rule --- today's connection practice --- and reports, separately, that without any interface rule the transmission network cannot accept the distribution exchange in 1 of 12 (passive) and 8 of 12 (price-taker) representative blocks (Sections~3.5 and~4.4). Because the coordinated arrangement is not restricted, we also re-evaluated it with the same no-reverse-flow rule imposed on the consensus exchange: the restriction raises its cost by 20.5~k\euro{}, 0.02\,\% of the 90.9~M\euro{} saving, so the 12.2\,\% benefit does not depend on the interface restriction (Section~4.4).
